                 TEXAS SOUTHWEST COUNCIL – BOY SCOUTS OF AMERICA’S
                                   REPLY BRIEF

TO THE HONORABLE ADMINISTRAVE LAW JUDGES:

            NOW COMES the Texas Southwest Council – Boy Scouts of America (TSWC-BSA) with

its Reply Brief in the above-referenced proceeding.

            1.     TSWC-BSA (Party No. 660) asks the ALJs and the Public Utility Commission of

Texas (the Commission) to NOT locate the Applicant’s 765-kV electric transmission line through

TSWC-BSA’s ranch in southwestern Menard County. Moreover, no party has advocated locating

the Applicant’s 765-kV electric transmission line through TSWC-BSA’s ranch.

            2.     The Applicants labeled TSWC-BSA’s potentially affected tracts as Tract Nos. 531,

532, 535, 536, and 537.1 Link P42 is the only link crossing TSWC-BSA’s ranch.2 That link is a part



1 See Oncor & LCRA-TSC Ex. 1, Att. 12 at 374.

2 See id.

SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349

 of Routes 266, 304, 376, 739, 910, 911, and 913.3 Those routes were not included in the Appli-

cants’ Routes of Interest Map referenced frequently at the hearing on the merits.4 And no party

has advocated for any of those routes in their initial briefs.

            3.    TSWC-BSA supports the Applicants’ “best meets” Route 894. TSWC-BSA specif-

ically opposes all the southern routes (e.g., Routes 295, 296, 572, and CCG) in the study area.

TSWC-BSA does not oppose locating this 765-kV electric transmission line on Routes 392, 410,

or 894 Western Mod 1.

            4.    In conclusion, TSWC-BSA asks the ALJs and the Commission to not locate the

Applicants’ 765-kV electric transmission line on its ranch. TSWC-BSA further asks for all other

relief it is justly entitled to.
